glosses: to offshore (moving an industrial production from one region to another or from one country to another, usually seeking lower business costs, like labor)
Déplacer une entreprise d'un pays vers un autre pour profiter d'une main d'œuvre moins coûteuse et réduire les coûts de production.

examples.text: Qu'est-ce qui perturbe, en priorité les intelligences, […] ; l'angoisse suscitée par une mondialisation qui délocalise le travail en même temps qu'elle désidentitarise les travailleurs ; […].

glosses: To transfer the management or day-to-day execution of a business function to a third-party service provider.

examples.text: They decided to outsource the design and manufacture of the system to a vendor.
Read said maintenance would be outsourced, with "positive discussions" held with two companies.

glosses: to move (something) from one place to another.

examples.text: We had to relocate the magazine rack because we bruised our shins on it too frequently when it was near the door.
HS2 will pass in a deep cutting, right through a busy road junction which has to be relocated.

glosses: to change one's domicile or place of business.

examples.text: Alfred relocated to Colorado Springs to take advantage of the boom in the defense industry.

On 'prosperity re-distribution', it ignores the prospect that businesses may relocate to be near HS2 stations. So never mind the observable phenomenon of major businesses relocating to Birmingham, with a veritable rash of private sector investment.
Approximately 100 Louisville-based KFC corporate employees will relocate to Texas over the next six months.

glosses: to lose something and find it again.

examples.text: I relocated the bird I spotted last week.
